title: Team USA soars above rivals to defend mixed team aerials Olympic gold
content:
Team USA once again soared above all others to win mixed team aerials gold and with it set a new American Winter Olympics record.

Four years after topping the podium in the inaugural competition in Beijing, the U.S. trio of Kaila Kuhn, Connor Curran and Christopher Lillis beat out Switzerland and China to take the title once more.

Lillis, the sole remaining member of the victorious 2022 team and now a double Olympic champion, delivered again, his back double full-full-full on the third and final jump crowning a dominant performance (325.35).

The gold is an 11th for the U.S. at the Milan Cortina Games, a new American record, surpassing the 10 they won on home soil in Salt Lake City 24 years ago.

Victory marks something of a redemption for Kuhn, who had to accept a fifth-place finish in the women’s event, with gold by far representing the high point of Curran’s young career.

Switzerland (296.91) grabbed silver while the Chinese team, which included husband-and-wife individual gold medalists Wang Xindi and Xu Mengtao, had to settle for bronze (279.68).

Kuhn sought out hypnosis to deal with her fear of the triple kicker but stuck her back full-full-full in the final round before Curran landed his back full-double full-full with a flourish.

“It was a super high-scoring event for the women and I was so happy to be in the mix. But that being said, I wanted to walk away with a medal, and I didn’t,” Kuhn said of her disappointment in the women’s competition.

“I let myself be upset for a couple of hours but I knew I had to switch gears. I wasn’t going to let that beat me down for too long. I just let that motivate me for my jumps today.”

Li Tianma’s failure to land his final jump for China made Lillis’ jump for glory more of a formality but he left nothing to chance, landing perfectly to spark golden celebrations even before the judges’ scores were confirmed.

“Team China is always the team to beat, it’s been that way for a little bit now,” Lillis said. “We were underdogs four years ago, I hope we weren’t the underdogs today, but I don’t know. They’re extremely talented athletes and it takes everything to beat them.

“They did help us a little bit with a few missteps. Any time we go into a team event, China is the number one team we’re looking to take down.”

The U.S. had earlier qualified first for the final with a huge 351.23 combined score after three more clean runs as rivals around them faltered.

Canada missed out on the final round alongside Ukraine and Kazakhstan with Australia, who counted individual silver medalist Danielle Scott in their team, progressing only to end up fourth.
